en.headline: Police find no evidence after Tuen Mun report of planned dog killing
en.dek: Animal-welfare volunteers called officers after a resident said she overheard talk of slaughtering a red-collared dog in So Kwun Wat; a search of a village house found nothing.
body: Police classified a suspected animal-cruelty report in So Kwun Wat, Tuen Mun, as a miscellaneous matter after a search of a village house on Tuesday night found no evidence that a dog had been killed or eaten.

The Animal Welfare Advocacy Alliance said it received a public tip at about 6pm that a beekeeper on So Kwun Wat Tsuen Road had claimed he would kill a dog wearing a red collar that evening and invite villagers to eat it. Volunteers who went to the area said they heard a single dog cry, then silence, and called the police.

Officers said they received a report at 9.42pm alleging that someone in the area was killing an animal for food. They entered a house and, after inspection, said they found no supporting evidence. No arrest was announced. The alliance and a resident who said she overheard the conversation have asked neighbours to stay alert for the missing animal.

zh.headline: 屯門掃管笏傳有人擬殺狗食用 警搜屋後無發現
zh.dek: 動物團體接報指村內有人揚言宰殺戴紅頸帶狗隻，義工聞狗吤報案；警方進入村屋調查，未發現殺狗或食狗證據，列雜項處理。
body: 屯門掃管笏周二晚傳出懷疑有人打算殺狗食用，動物福利關注聯盟接獲市民舉報後報警，警方其後進入一間村屋調查，表示未發現相關證據，案件列作雜項處理。
聯盟指晚上約6時接報，指掃管笏村路一名養蜂人士聲稱會於當晚殺死一隻戴紅色頸帶的狗，並邀請村民一同食用。義工到場後稱聽到一聲狗吤，其後再無聲響，遂報警。
警方表示晚上9時42分接獲報案，指該帶有人殺害動物作食用，人員進入單位搜查後，暫未有證據顯示有人在上址殺害或食用狗隻。警方未有公布拘捕行動。
